subject: SKU visibility, list-price parity, and reseller-netback sequencing
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@stellarnet.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SKU mapping & list-price parity — initial ask

Olga / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here is pulling together the marketplace path for our coming private offer. A few quick asks so we can align with our internal channel team: 

- We need SKU-level visibility: what exact SKU names will appear in AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace listings vs the private-offer line items. Our billing team requires mapping to reconcile partner invoices.
- List-price parity: will the marketplace list price be identical to the private-offer list price (we expect yes, but need to validate how early-phase promotional pricing will appear).
- Reseller netback sequencing: our partners expect a 12% netback on committed spend; we need confirmation on whether passback runs monthly or quarterly and who receives line-item credit in the invoice path.

Can you send a short mapping and a proposed cadence for passback? If you can attach a SKU matrix that shows list price vs private price and the proposed channel split, that would be perfect.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Cloud Procurement, StellarNet
procurement@stellarnet.com
[Attachment: internal-rfq-brief.pdf (pdf, 36KB)]

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@stellarnet.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SKU mapping & list-price parity — initial ask

Alicia —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers up front:

- SKU visibility: Redwood will publish marketplace SKUs that map 1:1 to the private-offer line items for billing reconciliation. We’ll include both the marketplace SKU and the private-offer item name in the item description so your finance team can match them.
- List-price parity: by default list price will match, but we can surface a short-lived promotional override ("welcome credit") that shows as a line-item discount in the private-offer invoice only — the marketplace list price remains the canonical amount for display.
- Reseller netback sequencing: passback options we support are monthly (default) or quarterly (for enterprise schedules). We’ll tag the partner line item in the invoice so your partner receives a dedicated credit row; the actual cash flow is handled by your reseller arrangement.

Attaching a first-pass SKU matrix and proposed terms. Ben / Irene — please review and flag any channel accounting caveats (I’ve thrown together conservative passback examples).

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Deal Ops, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_sku_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: review SKU matrix + channel margin notes

Quick internal note —

I reviewed the SKU matrix. Key points we should tighten before sending back to Alicia: 

1) Promo visibility: if we include a "welcome credit" as an invoice-only discount, confirm whether StellarNet's auditors will require a separate ledger event. If yes, we need to add a promo_code_id to the line item.

2) Channel margin: proposal in matrix currently shows 12% reseller netback on committed list price. Suggest we change to 10% guaranteed + a 2% accelerated commit rebate that vests after hitting a $1.2M quarterly threshold. This reduces short-term cash exposure and preserves an upside for StellarNet partners.

3) Passback cadence: default monthly is operationally simpler for us. Quarterly requires reconciliation windows we don’t have set up for this partner yet. Recommend proposing monthly passback but allow StellarNet to opt into quarterly in contract.

Marcus — can you confirm whether tagging the partner line item (for the marketplace invoice) will flow through the GCP invoice export we already produce? If not, we need engineering work.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Marketplace Sales

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: review SKU matrix + channel margin notes

Ben / team —

Checked the GCP export: current pipeline includes sku_id, display_price, and partner_tag fields. We do not currently export a separate promo_code_id; adding that is a short engineering task (estimated 2 sprints) because we need to thread it through invoicing and the private-offer rendering. Monthly partner-tagged credits are supported today.

Operational ask: if we move to a 10% guaranteed + 2% accelerator structure, we should document threshold logic precisely (e.g., whether threshold is measured at invoice date or usage settlement). I recommend "quarterly settlement trigger, monthly accrual" — that way partners see accruals monthly and settlement happens quarterly. That hybrid model reduces disputes.

Irene — please add a line in the terms pdf that clarifies accrual vs settlement.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Product Manager, Billing

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@stellarnet.com>, Tim Shaw <tim.shaw@stellarnet.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: SKU mapping + proposed passback cadence (attachment)

Alicia / Tim —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is an updated SKU matrix and a short private-offer term sheet showing the channel margin construct we propose: 10% guaranteed reseller netback + 2% accelerator that vests on a quarterly $1.2M commit. Highlights: 

- Marketplace list price will remain the canonical list price; promotional credits will appear as invoice-only discounts in the private-offer path.
- SKU mapping: each private-offer line includes marketplace_sku and private_item_name for reconciliation (see matrix).
- Passback cadence: monthly accrual with quarterly settlement (partner sees monthly accrual rows; credits applied quarterly).
- Technical note: Marcus confirmed partner_tag flows through current GCP export; adding promo_code_id requires a short engineering effort (we've noted it in the term sheet).

Next steps: if this structure looks good, can your procurement team confirm whether monthly accrual + quarterly settlement meets StellarNet's compliance needs and whether the partner netback structure is acceptable? If approved, we’ll prepare a DocuSign and include the engineering deliverable in the implementation SOW.

Attachments:
- proposed-private-offer-terms.pdf (pdf, 18 pages)
- redwood_sku_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Deal Ops, Redwood Inference
[Link to draft DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/preview/SN-2026-0829]
